title: Oceans and Forests Have Absorbed Roughly Half Our Carbon Emissions for Decades, Slowing Climate Change. But Can They Keep It Up? - Nautilus
author: Eric J. Morgan
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentOceans and Forests Have Absorbed Roughly Half Our Carbon Emissions for Decades, Slowing Climate Change. But Can They Keep It Up?Oceans and land have been absorbing a lot of the carbon emissions humans createEMAWAMBy Eric J. Morgan, Andrew J. Watson, and Andrew C. Manning11:00 AM CST on November 21, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleOver the past two centuries, humans have pumped billions of tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere by burning fossil fuels, raising global temperatures in the process.Luckily for humanity, Earth has done what it could to soften the impact.The world’s oceans have absorbed 35% of carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels since 1990, our new research shows, and the forests and other plants of the world have absorbed another 13%.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
